analysis.summary_cn: arXiv 论文提出 EarthRecord 基准，用 56 个站点、四十年 Landsat、MODIS、VIIRS 与 Sentinel-2 原始多传感器影像，评测多模态 Agent 的陆地变化分析能力。基准含 238 个问题、十类任务，云掩膜与跨传感器协调留给 Agent。测试十二个多模态 Agent 发现，多数能端到端完成，但从影像映射到地面真实变化仍弱，单卫星数据被改动后约半数正确答案随之改变。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.12934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. Two controls test what answers rest on: the closed book removes the record, and instrument pairs alter one satellite's data while nothing changes on the ground. Evaluations of twelve multimodal agents reveal that leading agents complete most analyses end to end but falter when an answer requires mapping from imagery. Further analysis shows that the record moves answers from prior knowledge to the pixels but not yet to the real change on the ground: when one satellite's data are altered, half of the right answers follow the alteration. EarthRecord thus provides a principled platform for measuring and advancing agents from pixels to land change.
title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.12933v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision provenance and characterizes the division of cognitive labor. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. Provenance showed that 59-68% of error corrections involved multiple participants and that about half of all decisions incorporated the input of another participant. These results may guide design principles for multi-agent scientific systems and inform future agent harnesses, model training, and accessible autonomous experimentation.
title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation

analysis.summary_cn: 该 arXiv 论文提出「能力回路」框架（IKC+KC+C），将智能体的现实影响拆为智能中介发现、程序性知识与直接控制三条路径。作者用 NK 适应度景观模拟验证：智能驱动的加速受限于竞争智能水平之比，而非任务难度；真正有效的安全杠杆是限制控制权与知识边界，而非单纯限制智能，并主张在架构中刻意「把物理纳入回路」。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.12941v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomously acting AI agents makes the governance of agentic systems urgent. We propose the competence circuit, summarized as IKC + KC + C, that decomposes an agent's real-world impact into three pathways: intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. Using the canonical fast-takeoff debate as a stress test, we formalize the conditions for intelligence-mediated fast takeoff as a conjunction jointly sufficient for fast catastrophic supremacy, showing that most rely on rapid knowledge acquisition or control attainment rather than intelligence alone. We operationalize epistemic intelligence as hypothesis-selection efficiency and validate this framework via stochastic simulation on NK fitness landscapes across six scenarios spanning the conjunctive chain. An analytic bound supported by the simulations shows that intelligence-driven speedup is capped by the ratio of competing intelligence levels regardless of task difficulty. The simulations also expose a fast-takeoff dilemma: a large intelligence-driven speedup multiplier materializes only when the hypothesis space is noisy, but the absolute timescale remains constrained by the time required for capability-critical tests, so a large multiplier need not imply rapid progress. Simulations also indicate that institutional chokepoints disproportionately slow down superintelligent agents when mandatory authorization delays are large relative to the negligible time these agents spend on unproductive search. We argue that the dominant safety levers are restricting control and enforcing knowledge boundaries rather than limiting intelligence alone, and this applies to agentic systems at any capability level. Purely digital domains weaken these bottlenecks, strengthening the case for architectures that intentionally "put physics in the loop."
title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence

analysis.summary_cn: 该论文研究多模态扩散语言模型（MDLM）的幻觉问题，发现迭代去噪中掩码不确定性总体下降，但少数步骤出现与幻觉相关的局部熵尖峰。据此提出 StepRefine，一种即插即用解码策略：在熵尖峰步骤用概率加权嵌入保留多元推理假设并做多轮连续精修，再通过精修控制器监测分布稳定性，及时切回离散去噪。多基准实验显示其可显著缓解幻觉。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.12901v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window. We hypothesize that discrete token commitment discards the distributional information at masked positions, limiting the continued interaction between candidate semantics and the context during entropy spikes. With this goal, we present StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding strategy that leverages semantic context to achieve reliable denoising. The core of our method lies in a step-aware switch between discrete denoising and latent refinement. The model employs probability-weighted embeddings at entropy spike steps to preserve diverse reasoning hypotheses and performs multiple rounds of continuous refinement. Meanwhile, a refinement controller monitors distributional stability to reduce unnecessary loops and switch the model back to standard discrete denoising. Through extensive experiments, StepRefine demonstrates significant hallucination mitigation across different MDLMs on multimodal benchmarks.
title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding

analysis.summary_cn: Every healthcare organization is working to deliver great care to more people at a lower cost. However, a general AI model is not enough to solve this

raw_summary:
Every healthcare organization is working to deliver great care to more people at a lower cost. However, a general AI model is not enough to solve this challenge. Today, healthcare runs on fragmented data. Patient records, coverage policies, and clinical evidence remain trapped across disconnected records, claims systems, and administrative tools that don’t work together. Clinicians are forced to spend nearly 28 hours a week on manually reconciling information, and patients wait for answers about their care and their coverage.

Healthcare organizations need a single, secure, governed orchestration layer that coordinates work across the systems they already run, assembling verifiable evidence and taking multi-step workflows through to completion with human oversight.

Today, we are announcing Gemini for healthcare. This purpose-built industry solution extends the universal Gemini agent, we introduced last month at Gemini at Work. 

The Gemini agent is a single, always-on agent for work where employees delegate an objective, and the agent plans the steps, retains organizational context, and routes across the best models to deliver finished outcomes inside the tools teams already use. The Gemini agent is built with enterprise-grade identity administration, fine-grained access control, and centralized policy management directly into its runtime. Every agent operates with a distinct identity, inherits each user’s existing role-based permissions, and enforces strict need-to-know boundaries across every user, sub-agent, and workflow. 

Working across clinical, financial, and administrative systems, it orchestrates multi-step tasks without forcing teams to switch applications:

  • For providers: Gemini provides a patient’s history across care settings, charts are prepared before the visit, and authorization packets are assembled against payer policy before submission, so fewer claims come back denied.

  • For health plans and payers: Gemini ensures requests are checked against medical policy and organized for the clinical reviewer, and benefits and costs are explained to members from their own plan documents.

Gemini for healthcare is built to support HIPAA compliance, with governance running underneath it all. It’s available starting today in preview.

Four components of Gemini for healthcare

Developed alongside clinical and health plan leaders, Gemini for healthcare provides an integrated, fully governed environment configured for payers and providers with four core components:

  1. Skills for healthcare work: Skills are reusable instructions and context, written by domain experts, that teach Gemini to run a specific task. Purpose-built, multi-step instructions guide the Gemini agent through essential clinical and administrative tasks, such as medical records synthesis, pre-appointment preparation, coverage and policy review, and payer benefit determination. Each skill applies your organization’s policies and plan rules, and teams can build custom skills tailored to the workflows and standard operating procedures unique to their organization.

  2. Connectors to clinical, financial, and operational systems: A library of connectors links Gemini directly to the EHR, claims, care management, and administrative systems organizations already run. Gemini queries each system while strictly preserving existing identity and role-based access controls, so teams get unified context without migrating sensitive data or altering permissions.

  3. An open healthcare partner ecosystem: Every health system and health plan runs a different mix of systems. Healthcare systems integrators and digital health partners help organizations extend Gemini with specialized solutions, connect it to what they already run, and scale it without lock-in.

  4. A secure, governed platform with open model choice: Clinical, security, and IT leaders get one place to set and enforce policies that govern every agent interaction. It is built to support HIPAA compliance, with enterprise-grade access controls, end-to-end audit logging, and verifiable citations so reviewers can check where each answer came from. Because the agent supports model choice, organizations can pair frontier models from Google and leading partners for complex clinical reasoning with fast, cost-efficient models for routine administrative steps under the same governance.

Unlocking high-value workflows with skills designed for payers and providers

Gemini for healthcare takes on the heavy assembly and administrative work that slows down clinical decisions and coverage determinations. 

At the point of care:

  • Building a longitudinal timeline from fragmented sources:  Synthesizes EHR and external records, separates active problems from resolved ones, lists allergies, and flags medication discrepancies. Clinicians get a grounded and unified patient picture in minutes rather than piecing together history across disconnected systems.

  • Reclaiming preparation time between patients: Prepares the patient chart ahead of a scheduled visit or procedure, flagging interval events, current medications, and outstanding clearances, labs, or consents, so care teams walk in with the full picture.

  • Streamlining clinical authorization and appeals: Extracts relevant chart evidence into an audit-ready packet for review, aligned with payer policy, flagging documentation gaps before submission rather than after a denial. If denials do occur, and the record supports it, it drafts an appeal grounded directly in the clinical record and the plan’s policy.

At the point of coverage:

  • Accelerating payer review: Checks incoming requests against the health plan’s medical policies and organizes the findings for reviewers, with findings traceable to the submitted documentation and coverage policy. Clinical reviewers spend less time assembling files and more time applying professional judgment.

  • Demystifying benefits and patient financial liability: Parses complex plan benefit booklets to estimate out-of-pocket costs, track deductibles, and verify in-network status, giving member services staff a step-by-step breakdown grounded in the member’s actual plan documents. For Medicare Advantage members, it applies Medicare’s coverage criteria where a plan’s internal rule is stricter.

Open ecosystem of connectors across the healthcare tech stack

Gemini for healthcare connects directly to core clinical, operational, and industry systems via secure connectors, inheriting each source system’s existing role-based access controls and data permissions.

EHRs and clinical data integration:

  • Epic EHR: Gives authorized users read-only access to patient conditions, medications, labs, clinical notes, and specialist documentation. With no write-back to the underlying chart, clinical data integrity remains completely intact.
  • Oracle Health EHR: Surfaces read-only patient histories, diagnostics, lab results, and clinical documentation for authorized users while enforcing zero write-back to ensure data integrity for the system of record.
  • InterSystems FHIR Server: Extending beyond EHR integrations, InterSystems FHIR MCP Server provides standardized, high-performance FHIR repository management and clinical data interoperability.
  • Verato: Resolves patient identity and matches records across visits and sources.
  • Keragon - Healthcare Integrations: Provides connectivity to 400+ healthcare applications, including EHRs, enabling organizations to securely connect their existing healthcare systems through a single MCP integration.

Eligibility, claims, and pricing:

  • Optum Coordination of Benefits: Finds additional patient coverage and determines the correct order of benefits before billing. Currently in limited release and testing with Gemini for Healthcare. 
  • Optum Network Eligibility: Retrieves patient eligibility and benefit details from connected health plans in real time. Currently in limited release and testing with Gemini for Healthcare.
  • TriZetto Provider Solutions: Verifies patient eligibility, coverage, co-pays, and deductibles across Medicare, Medicaid, and major commercial plans via TriZetto's vast network.
  • GoodRx: Enables care teams to discover prescription pricing and savings options, including manufacturer-sponsored self-pay programs, directly within AI-powered workflows to help patients access more affordable medications.
  • Infinitus Relay: Automates high-volume payer phone calls required for prior authorization and benefit verification.

Terminology and coding:

  • IMO Health: Brings terminology normalization, clinical search, and knowledge graphs into healthcare skills and governed agentic workflows.
  • ICD-10 Codes: Searches and validates ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes, billable status, and hierarchy.
  • RxNorm Drug Vocabulary: Looks up standardized drug names, ingredients, strengths, dose forms, and NDCs.

Coverage and provider reference:

  • CMS Coverage: Connects directly to Medicare coverage rules, National and Local Coverage Determinations (NCDs/LCDs), ensuring coverage reasoning rests on current published policy rather than static model knowledge.
  • NPPES NPI Registry: Verifies provider identity, clinical taxonomy, and practice location in real time.

Evidence based guidelines:

  • Optum EvidenceVue: Turns real-world clinical data into actionable evidence through AI-powered workflows from Optum Life Sciences. 
  • BMJ Digital Health: Delivers expert-curated, structured, peer-reviewed clinical guidelines and evidence, grounding care and coverage decisions in verifiable citations.

Clinical and operational workflows:

  • Salesforce: Headless Salesforce Health Cloud integrations bring workflows, data models, and Agentforce into Gemini for governed action right in the flow of work.
  • Suki: Delivers Ambient Clinical Intelligence across healthcare workflows, transforming clinical conversations into actionable intelligence that powers documentation, coding, revenue cycle management, and clinical reasoning.
  • UiPath: Connects healthcare-ready UiPath automations and agents to help teams assemble citation-backed context for operational reviews, prior authorizations, and appeals.
  • Synthpop Careflow: Orchestrates the patient journey across referral intake, coverage verification, and patient follow-up, turning unstructured referrals into validated, payer-ready orders without manual re-entry.
  • Alteryx: Enables healthcare teams to turn their domain expertise into automated analytics workflows, grounding AI-driven insights in business rules and calculations that are visible, understandable, repeatable, and auditable.

Enterprise productivity and collaboration:

  • Sana from Workday: Connects HR, finance, and enterprise knowledge so healthcare teams can surface policies, coordinate tasks, and get work done across administrative systems.
  • ServiceNow: Tracks IT incidents, operational service requests, and approval chains while enforcing existing enterprise routing rules.
  • Microsoft 365: Integrates directly with Word, Outlook, and SharePoint so prepared authorization packets, appeal letters, and benefit breakdowns land directly in the tools where teams already work.
  • Google Workspace: Connects seamlessly with Google Docs, Gmail, Drive, and Sheets to surface internal files and coordinate administrative workflows while enforcing enterprise access controls.

Security and compliance:

  • Cyera Dataport: Integrates with Cyera for data and agent security, delivering protected health information (PHI) context to support HIPAA audits and compliance reporting.

Global implementation partners and ecosystem

Through our open platform, organizations can deploy specialized partner agents such as ASCO Oncology Guideline Assistant or work with healthcare systems integrators, including 66degrees, Accenture, Altimetrik, AuxoAI, Cognizant, Deloitte, Egen, HCLTech, KPMG, NTT DATA, PwC, Quantiphi, Slalom, Tata Consultancy Services, TEKsystems Global Services, and Wipro, to customize, integrate, and scale these capabilities across complex enterprise architectures without vendor lock-in.

Developed alongside leading healthcare organizations

Health systems, health plan providers, academic medical centers, and clinical leaders are already working with Google Cloud to shape and apply these capabilities across care delivery, plan operations, and medical research: 

Synthesizing patient context at the point of care

  • “Making it easier for physicians to access and understand a patient’s medical history helps them spend less time gathering information and more time focused on patient care. Through our work with Google Cloud, we’re exploring how Gemini can interpret and synthesize complex patient information from multiple electronic health record systems and care settings, connecting data from different sources to give clinicians a more complete and cohesive understanding of a patient’s medical history.” — Michael J. Schlosser, MD, MBA, FAANS, Executive Vice President and Chief Clinical Officer, HCA Healthcare.

  • “Healthcare generates enormous amounts of information and data every day, yet patients often experience care as a series of separate interactions rather than one connected journey. Through our work with Google Cloud, we're exploring how AI can help connect information across the healthcare experience, making it easier to support the whole person, create more personalized care experiences, and equip clinicians with meaningful insights at the right time.” — Karen Hanlon, President, Highmark Health.

  • "By leveraging Gemini for healthcare, we will be able to use technology in a way that elevates the patient experience and strengthens the relationship between caregivers and those they serve. Through these integrated solutions, we expect to ease some of the administrative burden on our clinical teams and give them more time for what matters most: caring for their patients. Technology is at its best when it supports our caregivers and strengthens the human connection that is at the heart of healthcare." — Dr. John D'Angelo, President and CEO, Northwell Health.

Streamlining coverage, benefits, and payer operations

  • “The real promise of AI in healthcare isn’t simply doing today’s work faster. It’s creating a better way for the health system to work. When payers and providers can connect data, insights and workflows more seamlessly, we can remove unnecessary complexity, improve performance and help the entire system work better.” — Sandeep Dadlani, Chief Executive Officer, Optum Insight.

  • “Gemini for healthcare serves as a foundation for our unified architecture of reusable AI agents, enabling us to deliver new capabilities and productivity gains significantly faster than traditional development cycles. Our focus going forward is an agentic-AI model, where an intelligence layer drives deeper automation and operational transformation. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts is working toward that future in healthcare with Google Cloud." — Prem Somasundaram, Chief Information Officer, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts.

Accelerating clinical research and evidence-based guidelines

  • “For oncology care providers, quick access to current and relevant information is not a luxury, but a necessity. We are excited about what Gemini for healthcare could do to help care providers quickly find the critical information they need, when they need it, so they can drive better outcomes for patients.” — Clifford Hudis, MD, FACP, FASCO, Chief Executive Officer, American Society of Clinical Oncology.

Built on an enterprise-grade foundation

Google is both a frontier AI lab and an enterprise cloud. Gemini for healthcare runs on Google Cloud’s secure infrastructure and is built to support HIPAA compliance. Clinical data, prompts, and generated outputs remain within your organization’s governed environment and are never used to train or fine-tune Google’s foundation models. Outputs are grounded in clinical records, plan policies, and your organization’s approved guidelines and evidence, with traceable citations and audit logging that give clinical, compliance, and IT leaders visibility and control. And because we operate the full stack, from infrastructure and models through security and the application layer, we can optimize performance, reliability, and cost together, routing high-volume administrative tasks to fast, low-cost models and reserving high-reasoning models for complex clinical and operational analysis, so organizations can scale AI across the enterprise without scaling spend at the same rate.

This is just the beginning

The launch of Gemini for healthcare marks another step in our commitment to bring the best of Gemini to every professional and every workflow, natively tailored to the way their industry works.

Gemini for healthcare is available in preview in the U.S. today, joining our expanding suite of purpose-built solutions for legal, financial services, and government services. We invite leaders across health systems, medical groups, health plan providers, and payers to explore how Gemini can transform their most critical clinical and operational workflows.
source: Google Cloud AI and Machine Learning Blog
title: Introducing Gemini for healthcare

analysis.summary_cn: arXiv 论文提出稀疏目标优化（STO），关注知识编辑中目标隐藏态构造阶段：理论证明参数空间干扰与目标隐藏态干扰正相关，故对知识向量施加 L1 正则剪除冗余枝杈，只保留核心分量，从而降低单次编辑对其他知识的影响。多模型与基准实验验证有效，代码已开源。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.12995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Knowledge editing has emerged as a promising approach for efficiently updating embedded knowledge in large language models (LLMs). It first computes an ideal target hidden state that steers the LLM toward the new output, and then edits the model parameters so that the original hidden state is mapped to this target. While most existing methods focus on the second stage of parameter editing in preserving other knowledge, we find that the upstream construction of the target hidden state also plays an important role in allocating the model's limited capacity space. We first establish a theoretical connection between interference in the parameter space and interference between target hidden states, showing that the two are positively correlated. Building on this insight, we propose a simple yet effective $\ell_1$ regularization method that prunes away unnecessary ``tentacles'' of each knowledge vector, retaining only the essential components. With fewer extraneous tentacles, each edit affects less other knowledge, enabling better coexistence. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and benchmark datasets verify the effectiveness of our method. Code: https://github.com/wintersdragon-c/STO.
title: Capacity Allocation at the Source: Sparse Target Optimization for LLM Knowledge Editing

analysis.summary_cn: arXiv 论文提出 HiCAP 框架，将人格特质引入跨文化对话生成：先按文化语气对齐，再依据个体人格精炼语言表达与内容，采用监督微调加指令微调、动态指令模板与多智能体示例。在 CulturalPersonas 与 CPED 数据集上各项对话指标整体最优，显示文化适应性与人格建模有效。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.13207v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cultural adaptation in dialogue systems refers to the ability to generate responses that conform to linguistic norms and social expectations across different cultures. However, existing dialogue generation approaches pay limited attention to the role of personality in shaping cultural expression and communication style. We therefore propose HiCAP, a novel framework that integrates personality traits into culturally adaptive dialogue generation. HiCAP employs a personality-conditioned control mechanism that hierarchically modulates response style by first aligning it with the cultural tone and then refining linguistic expression and content according to individual personality attributes. To embed these factors, the model combines supervised fine-tuning and instruction-based tuning, supported by dynamic instruction templates and multi-agent demonstrations to capture diverse combinations of culture and personality. Experiments on CulturalPersonas and CPED show that HiCAP achieves the strongest overall performance across various dialogue generation metrics, demonstrating effective cultural adaptability and personality modelling.
title: HiCAP: Hierarchical Cultural Adaptation via Personality for Dialogue Generation

analysis.summary_cn: 该 arXiv 论文提出“定义敏感度”指标，用于衡量 LLM 在社会学概念标注任务中是否真正遵循提示里的定义。方法是对同一批文本用两个相互竞争的定义各标注一次，并将仅改写措辞、要求不变时的分歧作为“改写基线”。在六个概念、三个 LLM 上的实验显示，更换定义带来的标注变化始终高于改写基线，说明标注结果高度依赖所给定义，因此报告结果时应同时给出定义、定义敏感度和改写基线。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.13339v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In social science research, text annotation is a fundamental task that is traditionally a costly, hard-to-scale manual process. Researchers have used large language models (LLMs) to perform annotation by writing a definition of a concept into a prompt - a rule that determines whether a label should be attributed to a text depending on its content. However, concepts such as hate speech, fake news, and terrorism typically have several theoretically defensible competing definitions. It is also unknown whether the model actually applied the definition to provide the label or the label was based on the model's pretrained notion of the concept. To test this, we have the model annotate the same texts twice, each time with a different definition. We call the disagreement between the two sets of annotations definition sensitivity. As a control, we paraphrase one definition but leave its requirements unchanged - the disagreement between the annotations with the two wordings becomes the paraphrase floor. Across six concepts and three LLMs, a swap of competing definitions always changes more annotations, on average, than a paraphrase. This shows that the annotations depend on the prompted definition, so any set of annotations should be interpreted together with the definition that produced it. The LLM annotator's definition sensitivity and its paraphrase floor should both be reported in such work.
title: Measuring Definition Sensitivity in LLM Annotation of Social Science Concepts

analysis.summary_cn: 本文提出 TopicScope 框架，利用稀疏自编码器（SAE）特征训练因果主题分类器，在预填充阶段训练、解码生成阶段对每个 token 实时打主题标签，支持响应中途主题切换。在 Gemma-3 1B/4B 上，预填充特征训练的监控器可泛化至解码阶段，对插入离题内容、删主题、重排等扰动最多仅损失 5 个 macro-F1 点；消融显示无 SAE 需数倍规模模型才达基线。代码与数据集已开源。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.12935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. We also found that the classifiers are robust to perturbations, losing at most 5 macro-F1 points when off-topic asides are inserted, topics are removed or sections are reordered. Ablations conducted to understand the contribution of the SAE revealed that classifiers reaching baseline performance without it were several times larger. Our findings show that compact topic monitors can be trained inexpensively in prefill and deployed during generation. More broadly, our work shows where SAEs are useful beyond safety classification. Our code, dataset and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Mercity-AI/SAE-Guardrails and https://huggingface.co/collections/Mercity/online-guardrails-using-sparse-autoencoders-6ac602940468c62fefb2b9e8
title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring

analysis.action: read
analysis.reason: 来自arXiv的受控实验，来源可信度较高，且与用户关注的RAG/Agent推理相关，对多模态提示设计有实用指导；但属细分方向、增益有限，未达高优先级，建议阅读原文并关注自适应视觉提示策略。
analysis.summary_cn: 该arXiv论文研究在多模态大视觉语言模型的知识图谱问答(KGQA)中，文本提示加入图谱可视化图像的效果。基于WebQSP和CWQ共1500问题、六种VLM的受控评测显示，加入图图像平均提升1.85 F1，主要来自低复杂度问题的精确率提升(+4.65 F1)；增益不依赖模型规模，但对图形布局高度敏感，层级式Graphviz布局优于杂乱渲染，大子图拆分为独立路径收益最大，据此提出自适应视觉提示策略。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.12938v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Using a controlled evaluation over 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions and six VLMs within a fixed KGQA pipeline, we compare text-only prompting against text-plus-graph visualization at the per-question level and analyze performance changes as a function of reasoning complexity, model size, and image layout. Adding a graph image yields an average gain of 1.85 F1 points, driven by strong precision improvements on low-complexity questions (+4.65 F1). Mixed-effects and regression analyses show that these multimodal gains do not depend strongly on model scale, but are highly sensitive to graph layout: image-only settings sharply degrade performance, hierarchical Graphviz layouts outperform less organized renderings, and decomposing large subgraphs into separated paths yields the largest improvements. Taken together, the results indicate that visual prompting primarily aids KGQA by enhancing prediction precision in low-complexity contexts, provided that visual design respects cognitive and perceptual constraints. To optimize both accuracy and inference efficiency, we argue for adaptive visual prompting policies that selectively append diagrams to small, visually sparse subgraphs with well-structured layouts, avoiding unnecessary visual clutter and token overhead on complex queries. We conclude by relating these findings to a visual notation design theory, outlining how principled diagram encoding can guide future multimodal VLM prompting.
title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering

analysis.summary_cn: arXiv 新论文提出 Brasilidade 基准，用于评估大模型在巴西葡萄牙语上的能力，覆盖语言、语法与地域变体等四个领域，当前开放第一个领域的标准化任务。结果显示模型规模并不必然决定表现，多个中型模型超过更大模型；针对葡语专门训练的模型整体也未高于平均水平。任务难度分化明显，部分极易、部分极难，说明需专门基准暴露短板并指导后续训练。代码已开源。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.12906v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This work presents a new benchmark that aims to address the limitations of current methods for evaluating LLMs in Brazilian Portuguese. We introduced Brasilidade, an assessment methodology comprised of standardized tasks distributed across four different domains, and we are making available the tasks from its first domain, which address nuances of the language, grammar, and variations of Brazilian Portuguese. The results show that model size, by itself, does not determine performance; several medium-sized models outperformed larger models in the protocols evaluated. Specific models for Portuguese, in general, did not perform above average, despite their targeted training. Different task levels revealed significant nuances: while some tasks proved easy for most models, others posed extreme challenges, and some yielded mixed results, with wide variations in performance. This clearly illustrates the need for benchmarks that address the limitations of the models in Brazilian Portuguese, allowing future training cycles to seek to overcome them. Project repository https://github.com/soberania-oficial/brasilidade
title: Brasilidade: Measuring Brazilian Identity for Large Language Models

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.13366v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In teaching and learning environments, cheating and the violation of academic integrity have always been one of the challenges, involving different levels of concerns such as administrative, personal knowledge, learning, and equity. The introduction of large language models has brought cheating in dialogue to the forefront, given the apparent capabilities of these models to complete students' academic assignments. This study aims to leverage recent dialogues among university professors about cheating with Generative AI to better understand their beliefs about academic honesty. In doing so, we analyze a corpus of 2.01 million posts (threads and comments) in the r/Professors subreddit discussing cheating after the release of ChatGPT, providing a better understanding of teachers' motivations to discourage cheating and the strategies they use to do so. We synthesize the why and how of addressing cheating to identify caveats about the future of AI and academic integration.
title: Mapping Instructors' Attitudes Towards Cheating with AI: An Exploratory Analysis Using Forum Analysis

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.12936v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. Specifically, LandslideFM adapts to multiple visual tasks via a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning framework that leverages limited labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled data. Furthermore, predicted landslide regions provide explicit spatial guidance to a Vision-Language Model adapted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, enabling comprehensive landslide reasoning. To support training and evaluation in this domain, we also present LandslideVL, the first benchmark for intelligent landslide analysis, combining visual imagery and newly introduced textual prompts. Comprehensive experiments across public datasets and LandslideVL demonstrate that LandslideFM achieves superior quantitative and qualitative performance. Most importantly, LandslideFM surpasses general-purpose VLMs in specialized landslide reasoning and scene analysis. Our code is released at https://github.com/wangshanwen001/LandslideFM.
title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
